items.title: Calculation of Relative Molecular Mass (Mᵣ) of a Gas

source_refs.note: Calculation of Relative Molecular Mass (Mᵣ) of a Gas: a main subheading of 5.2 Ideal gas equation, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 97-97.

blocks.text: Equation (4) can be employed to calculate the relative molecular mass of a gas whose P, T, V and mass in grams are known. This is achieved by rearranging equation (4)
Putting n = m/M in equation (4) Where m = mass in g and M = molar mass of the gas
At molecular level, the molar mass becomes relative molecular mass of a compound, therefore, we can write

blocks.title: Sample Problem 5.1
blocks.problem: The volume of 134 g of a gas at -73 ℃ under 10 atm pressure is 5 dm³. Determine the relative molecular mass of the gas.
steps: Solution: The molecular mass of the gas can be calculated by using the formula: M = mRT/PV
M = (134 g)(0.0821 atm dm³ mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)(200 K) / (10 atm)(5 dm³)
blocks.answer: Therefore, the relative molecular mass of the gas is 44 amu.
